demo_test.yaml:
# Acceptance tests for demo — the CI gate for your control logic.
#
#   naut test          run them
#   naut test -v       with the virtual time each test covered
#   naut test -run re  just the ones whose name matches
#
# The fixture is nautilus.yaml: tasks, scan rates, tag roles and seeds all
# come from the manifest that deploys, so a test can never drift away from
# what actually runs. Retune Kp here and the tests retune with it.
#
# Time is VIRTUAL. `advance: 10s` runs ten seconds of process time in well
# under a millisecond, EXACTLY — so the 10 s alarm delay and the loop's
# settling time are ordinary things to assert, not things to hope about.
# None of this is possible against a wall clock.

tolerance: 0.5 # default ± for `near` in this file

tests:
  - name: pump seals in below the start level and drops out above it
    suspend: [sim] # freeze the plant — this test owns the level
    steps:
      - given: { LevelPct: 35.0 }
        scans: 1
        expect: { PumpRun: true }
      - given: { LevelPct: 60.0 } # between the bands — the seal-in holds
        scans: 1
        expect: { PumpRun: true }
      - given: { LevelPct: 80.0 }
        scans: 1
        expect: { PumpRun: false }

  - name: low-temp alarm waits its full 10 s
    suspend: [sim] # drive the temperature directly
    given: { TempC: 45.0 } # below the 62 °C cold threshold
    steps:
      - advance: 9.5s
        expect: { TempLowAlm: false } # the TON has not elapsed
      - advance: 1s
        expect: { TempLowAlm: true } # ... and now it has
      - given: { TempC: 70.0 }
        scans: 1
        expect: { TempLowAlm: false } # TON has no off-delay

  - name: PI settles a setpoint step and holds it
    # Closed loop: sim.st integrates the plant while the PI runs, both on
    # virtual dt. `until` + `hold` is the assertion a settling test needs —
    # a loop that merely passes through its target on the way to an
    # overshoot has not settled, and "assert after 45 s" cannot tell.
    steps:
      - until: 300s
        expect: { TempC: { near: 65.0 } }
      - given: { TempSP: 72.0 }
        until: 45s
        hold: 5s
        expect:
          # An ST expression, compiled by the same compiler as your logic —
          # for anything a fixed matcher cannot say. Reusable predicates go
          # in blocks.st as a FUNCTION returning BOOL.
          - ABS(TempC - TempSP) < 0.5
        always:
          Heater: { between: [0.0, 100.0] } # the clamp never breaks

  - name: high-temp interlock sounds the horn until the operator acks
    suspend: [sim]
    given: { TempC: 95.0 } # above the 90 °C trip in interlocks.ld
    steps:
      - advance: 4s
        expect: { HiTempAlm: false } # 5 s on-delay on the 200 ms task
      - advance: 1.5s
        expect: { HiTempAlm: true, Horn: true }
      - given: { HornAck: true }
        advance: 400ms
        expect:
          Horn: false
          HiTempAlm: true # acking the horn must not clear the alarm
      - given: { TempC: 60.0 } # both alarms clear → the ack self-releases
        advance: 1s
        expect: { HiTempAlm: false, HornAck: false }
nautilus.yaml:
# demo — a nautilus controller, no Go required.
#   naut run     scan loop + dashboard + tag API
#   naut test    acceptance tests in virtual time
#   naut check   compile (the CI gate)
#   naut build   emit a self-contained controller binary
#
# Three tasks, three IEC languages, one tag store — the resource/task model
# from the standard. Control in FBD, the annunciator in ladder, and even the
# PLANT PHYSICS simulated in ST, so this runs and moves with no hardware.
# Go remains the tier for real field buses and richer simulation:
# `naut new --template sdk-demo`.
name: demo

server:
  addr: "localhost:8080"   # NAUTILUS_ADDR overrides; set NAUTILUS_TOKEN to gate writes
  online-edits: true       # PLC-style online edits from VS Code (off for production)
  # hmi: ./hmi/build        # serve a built HMI at "/" instead of the dashboard —
                            # see "Serving the HMI from the controller" in the docs

# One program per task, each on its own scan. The FIRST task owns field I/O.
# dt-tag receives the measured scan-to-scan seconds — bind it wherever you
# integrate (PI loops, ramps, physics) instead of assuming the interval.
tasks:
  - program: program.fbd   # the control loop — pump seal-in + heater PI
    scan: 100ms
    dt-tag: ScanDtS
  - name: sim              # the plant, simulated in IEC (delete for real I/O)
    program: sim.st
    scan: 100ms
    dt-tag: SimDtS
  - name: interlocks       # the annunciator, in ladder
    program: interlocks.ld
    scan: 200ms

# Tags by role: input (driver → tag), output (tag → driver),
# setpoint (operator-writable, exists from scan one, kept across a restart
# by a retain: section), state (logic-owned; kept only with retain: true
# and a retain: section).
# unit/desc feed the dashboard's tag table and GET /api/meta.
tags:
  # process values — owned by the sim task here. For real I/O, delete the
  # sim task and make these `role: input` so the driver supplies them.
  - { name: LevelPct, role: state, init: 60.0, unit: "%",  desc: "Tank level" }
  - { name: TempC,    role: state, init: 60.0, unit: "°C", desc: "Tank temperature" }
  # operator setpoints — writable from the HMI/API from scan one
  - { name: TempSP,         role: setpoint, init: 65.0, unit: "°C", desc: "Temperature setpoint" }
  - { name: TempLowSP,      role: setpoint, init: 62.0, unit: "°C", desc: "Low temperature alarm threshold" }
  - { name: HiTempSP,       role: setpoint, init: 90.0, unit: "°C", desc: "High temperature alarm threshold" }
  - { name: Kp,             role: setpoint, init: 12.0, desc: "PI proportional gain" }
  - { name: Ki,             role: setpoint, init: 0.15, unit: "1/s", desc: "PI integral gain" }
  - { name: PumpStartLevel, role: setpoint, init: 40.0, unit: "%", desc: "Pump seal-in level" }
  - { name: PumpStopLevel,  role: setpoint, init: 75.0, unit: "%", desc: "Pump drop-out level" }
  - { name: HornAck,        role: setpoint, init: false, desc: "Horn acknowledge — releases when alarms clear" }
  # commands — sent to the driver (loopback here)
  - { name: PumpRun, role: output, init: false, desc: "Pump run command" }
  - { name: Heater,  role: output, init: 0.0, unit: "%", desc: "Heater output command" }
  # computed state — retained across scans and online edits
  - { name: TempLowAlm, role: state, init: false, desc: "Low temperature alarm (10 s delay)" }
  - { name: HiTempAlm,  role: state, init: false, desc: "High temperature alarm (interlocks.ld)" }
  - { name: Horn,       role: state, init: false, desc: "Annunciator horn (interlocks.ld)" }
  - { name: TempRate,   role: state, init: 0.0, unit: "°C/min", desc: "Temperature rate of change (blocks.st)" }

# memory = loopback for bring-up. For an Allen-Bradley Logix controller:
#   driver:
#     type: eip
#     host: 192.168.1.10
#     manifest: eip_manifest.yaml   # from `naut eip import`
driver:
  type: memory
interlocks.ld:
PROGRAM Interlocks
(* The annunciator as LADDER — a third language on the same tag store, on
   its own 200 ms task. Rung grammar: series = AND, [ a | b ] = OR branch,
   /x = NC contact, ( x ) coil, ( S x )/( R x ) latch/unlatch,
   FN(args) comparison contact, inst:TYPE(args) function block.

   Open the diagram: VS Code -> right-click interlocks.ld ->
   "Open With -> Ladder Diagram". With live values on, power flow paints
   the rungs as the plant runs. *)
VAR_EXTERNAL
    TempLowAlm : BOOL;
    TempC      : REAL;
    HiTempSP   : REAL;
    HornAck    : BOOL;
    Horn       : BOOL;
    HiTempAlm  : BOOL;
END_VAR
VAR
    HiSecs : TIME; (* how long we've been hot — captured via ET => *)
END_VAR
LD
  RUNG hitemp (* comparison as a contact, 5 s on-delay; ET captured with the standard's => output binding *)
    GT(TempC, HiTempSP) t1:TON(PT := T#5S, ET => HiSecs) ( HiTempAlm )

  // Comment runs like this render as notes in the ladder diagram —
  // double-click to edit them there.
  RUNG horn (* either alarm sounds the horn until the operator acks *)
    [ TempLowAlm | HiTempAlm ] /HornAck ( Horn )

  RUNG ackclear (* the ack releases itself once both alarms clear *)
    /TempLowAlm /HiTempAlm ( R HornAck )
END_LD
END_PROGRAM
